target_customer: Small and mid-sized companies that book hotels, flights and cars for employees and want negotiated rates
problem: Employees booked business travel on archaic booking sites or through agents that charged booking fees, and booking took a long time. Companies wanted corporate or group negotiated rates and cost tracking without heavy tools.
business_model: Free booking for companies, with revenue from integrations with employer HR and expense systems (per TechCrunch, 2015-02-24); later described as a business travel platform

founders.name: Wen-Wen Lam
founders.background_notes: YC page lists her as Founder/CEO and later Partner at Gradient Ventures. No education or prior employers found in sources opened.

founders.name: Alexey Pakhomov
founders.background_notes: YC page describes him as founder, biohacker and eco enthusiast. No other background found.

competitors.name: SAP Concur
competitors.what: Incumbent online corporate booking tied to expense reporting
competitors.traction_then: A 2017 survey put its US corporate booking share at 65 percent (later date than founding)

competitors.name: Traditional travel agents and booking sites with booking fees
competitors.what: Archaic booking websites and agents that charged fees; the article contrasts NexTravel with these
competitors.traction_then: Booking time cited as 80 minutes versus 20 to 30 with NexTravel (company claim)

technical_complexity.rationale: A booking front end over existing inventory and rate sources with HR and expense integrations; hard parts were rate access and integrations, not research-grade technology.

defensibility.rationale: Customers could switch booking tools, though integrations with HR and expense systems added some stickiness. Rate access depended on suppliers, not exclusive assets.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents kept dominating; NexTravel was eventually acquired by a better funded rival, TravelPerk, in January 2021.

market_need_then: TechCrunch (2015-02-24) quoted booking time falling from 80 minutes to 20 or 30 in many cases and described employers wanting simpler flight and hotel search with cost tracking. Corporate travel was a large, established spend.

branding.domain_note: Used nextravel.com; domain now redirects to perk.com (observed 2026-11).

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand itself was found; it was a descriptive compound name that was folded into Perk after acquisition.

outcome_analysis: NexTravel launched from YC W15 with a simple corporate booking pitch and served several hundred to about 700 customers including Yelp, Stripe and Harry's by its 2021 sale. It never became a category leader against Concur and later TripActions, and was acquired by TravelPerk in January 2021 with undisclosed terms, with founders and team joining the buyer.
notes: Funding unverified: aggregators (CB Insights, Seedtable, startupintros) show a 2015 seed of about $2M to $2.1M and a Series A of about $2.4M in 2020, with totals of $2.52M or $4.5M. TechCrunch (2021) cited $4.5M from Crunchbase. No primary source seen, so no round recorded. Founding year 2013 per TechCrunch 2021; YC lists 2013. Customer count about 700 and 300,000 trips per TechCrunch 2021. Perk invested in the acquisition round per CB Insights. UPDATE (completeness pass): the 2015 seed (about $2M) rests on StartupIntros and the 2020 Series A (about $2.4M) on database listings (CB Insights, Village), each a single database. TechCrunch (2021-01-13) says NexTravel raised about $4.5M per Crunchbase, which exceeds the recorded rounds, so some funding is unrecorded. CB Insights totals $2.52M over 5 rounds.
